E1.evidence: The source is the ROS 2 design article "ROS 2 Access Control Policies" (Ruffin White, Kyle Fazzari; written 2019-08, modified 2021-06), which "specifies the policy format used for access control when securing ROS subsystem." It defines the SROS 2 policy XML schema and its deny-by-default semantics ("allowing access to an object if and only if rules exist that allow a given subject to access the resource"). Its only failure-related content is design concerns stated in general terms, e.g. under Composability: "ROS 2 allows for the remapping of many namespaced subsystems at runtime ... While it is perhaps unreasonable to expect this dynamic flexibility from staticky provisioned permissions without allocating such capabilities prior, it should be made possible to infer the necessary capabilities from composed launch files". No concrete system, node pair, reproducer, error log, or maintainer confirmation of a defect is given.
